task: Prepare the Dell Precision T5810 and Quadro M4000 for measured gaming optimization

impact_map.problem: The Quadro M4000 was running as Microsoft Basic Display Adapter without an NVIDIA driver.
indirect_risks: Driver updates require a reboot and may reset NVIDIA profiles.
Overclocking is deferred until thermal and VRAM stability are measured.
impact_map.smallest_safe_change: Establish a stock-clock baseline, apply reversible Windows settings, and install measurement tools.
verification: OCCT GPU and VRAM stability tests

hardware.cpu: Intel Xeon E5-2690 v4 (14 cores / 28 threads)

vram_stress_test.termination: Stopped at the 55-second safety deadline because FurMark VRAM mode ignored max-time.

system_benchmarks.source: Windows System Assessment Tool formal assessment

bottlenecks.evidence: Three 16 GB RDIMMs and three 4 GB RDIMMs populate only six of eight slots; measured bandwidth is about 30 GB/s.
bottlenecks.recommended_fix: Use four matched 16 GB DDR4-2400 ECC RDIMMs across the four primary channel sockets for 64 GB quad-channel operation.

bottlenecks.evidence: FurMark holds about 119 W against a fixed 120 W limit while core clock falls below the 772 MHz application clock.
bottlenecks.recommended_fix: Prefer memory tuning and efficiency after the R535 driver update; do not use blind core overclocking.
Install the downloaded NVIDIA 539.19 WHQL package and reboot.

next_gate: Install 539.19 cleanly, reboot, rerun the baseline, then tune memory and efficiency against the saved stock result.
